sets.title: Technical clarity
sets.description: Long technical words are where speakers mumble. Hit the stressed syllable and finish every ending.
sets.tip: Slow down by 10% on the long words. Say every syllable you'd write.

items.text: Our asynchronous pipeline guarantees idempotent writes with very low latency.
The architecture uses Kubernetes to orchestrate containerized microservices.
We prioritized throughput over consistency for the analytics workloads.
Authentication and authorization are two separate responsibilities.
Better observability improved our reliability and scalability this quarter.

sets.title: Word stress
sets.description: English changes meaning and clarity with stress: PHOtograph, phoTOgraphy, photoGRAPHic. Wrong stress is the #1 reason clear speakers get misheard.
sets.tip: Make the stressed syllable longer, louder and higher. Relax the others.

items.text: The photographer loves photography, and this photograph is her favorite.
Before we analyze the data, let's read the analyst's analysis.
We record every record, and we will present the present status.
items.tip: Nouns stress the first syllable (REcord, PREsent); verbs stress the second (reCORD, preSENT).

items.text: The technology is technical, but the technician makes it simple.
Economics shapes the economy, and every economic decision matters.

sets.title: TH sounds
sets.description: TH is often replaced with s, t, d or f. Put the tip of your tongue lightly between your teeth and blow.
sets.tip: Voiceless TH (think) is just air; voiced TH (this) adds a buzz.

items.text: I think three things went through the thread on Thursday.
This is the theory they thought through together.
Thank you for thinking so thoroughly about the method.
Those were the months when the growth was healthy.

sets.title: V and W
sets.description: V uses your top teeth on your bottom lip. W uses rounded lips and no teeth.
sets.tip: For V, feel the buzz on your lip. For W, start like 'oo'.

items.text: Very well, we will review the video by Wednesday.
Our vision is to deliver value wherever we work.
The vendor's valuable advice was worth waiting for.

sets.title: R and L
sets.description: L touches the tongue tip behind the top teeth. R never touches; the tongue pulls back.
sets.tip: Say 'la-ra-la-ra' slowly and feel where the tongue goes.

items.text: Please collect the correct results early tomorrow.
The rollout rarely looks right on the first release.
Leadership is really about clear and reliable relationships.

sets.title: Short vs long vowels
sets.description: Short i (ship, live) is quick and relaxed. Long ee (sheep, leave) is longer, with a smile.
sets.tip: Exaggerate the length difference at first — it's the length listeners hear.

items.text: Please sit in this seat and fill in the field.
I will leave if you still live here.
We need to keep the team's big wins visible.

sets.title: Word endings
sets.description: Dropped endings (-ed, -s, -ts, -ks) make speech sound rushed and change meaning: 'asked' vs 'ask'.
sets.tip: Land the last sound of each word before moving on.

items.text: She asked six questions and listed the costs.
He walked, talked and worked through the last months.
The results helped us fix the products' biggest risks.
